At the origin the numerator is |-6| = 6, and the normal magnitude is sqrt(1 + 4 + 4) = 3. Thus the distance is 2.
Choose the cut vertices as (1,0,0), (0,1,0), and (0,0,1), giving plane x+y+z=1. The retained solid has x+y+z≥1, and the maximum sum is 3 at (1,1,1). Its height is therefore (3-1)/√3=2√3/3.

Regular tetrahedron vertices (+,+,+),(+,-,-),(-,+,-),(-,-,+) in coordinates +/-1 give R=sqrt(3), face distance r=1/sqrt(3). An exterior face-tangent sphere center is (r+rho)n. The furthest point from O has radius r+2rho; internal contact with the circum-ball gives r+2rho=R, so rho=r. Face normals have pairwise dot product -1/3; their centers 2r*n have pairwise distances 2r*sqrt(8/3)>2r. All four are internally tangent to the big sphere and externally tangent to the central sphere, so disjoint interiors give uniform volume ratio 5*(r/R)^3=5/27. Internal tangency is derived by the radial maximum, not imported from an external-tangency-only node.
